title: Abba bar Binyamin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived in Eretz Yisrael, in the city of Arbel (in the book Kaftor va-Feraḥ, the distance of Arbel is given as about half an hour from Tiberias). In [Jerusalem Talmud] Shevi'it ch. 6, end of halakhah 3, Rabbi Abbahu came to Arbel and was received by Abba bar Binyamin. We have already said that bet and mem are interchanged, so it is not far-fetched to say that he is the one mentioned in Gittin 29b under the name Abba bar Manyumi: someone sent a get via an agent and instructed him to give the get to Abba bar Manyumi, because he knows the woman. When the agent arrived, he found Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa, and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, and they said to him, 'Entrust your agency before us; when Abba bar Manyumi comes, we will give it to him.' But it is not reasonable to say that he is Abba the son of Rav Binyamin bar Ḥiyya, since the latter is always mentioned as 'the son of Rav Binyamin'; likewise, this is not the Abba bar Manyumi whom we always find together with the Babylonian amoraim.

notes.text: Hyman suggests bet/mem variation connects Binyamin and Manyumi, but expressly excludes two Babylonian namesakes.

Gittin 29b directly names Abbahu, Chanina bar Pappa and Yitzchak Nappacha, with Rav Safra present, and gives competing versions of the agency argument. Hyman’s Binyamin/Manyumi equation remains conjectural and his exclusions of two Babylonian namesakes remain explicit.
